Respondent :- Fudhi Bajpai And 2 Ors.

Counsel for Appellant :- Rajendra Jaiswal,Rajeev Mishra Hon'ble Jaspreet Singh,J.
1.

The instant appeal has been preferred under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 assailing the award dated 31.03.2003 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal/Additional District Judge, Court No.5, District Unnao in Claim Petition No.93 of 1999 whereby the claim petition came to be dismissed.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal/Additional District Judge, Court No.5, District Unnao
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Shri Rajendra Jaiswal, learned counsel for the appellant has urged that the Tribunal has erred in dismissing the claim petition solely on the ground that the P.W.2 who was examined and was stated to be an eye witness but since his name was not included in the list of witnesses in the chargesheet filed in respect of the FIR lodged relating to the accident in question, accordingly it created a doubt regarding the credibility of the witness.

It is urged that this was not a sufficient ground to have dismissed the claim petition rather the weight of the testimony of the said witness should have been Santosh Kumar And 3 Ors. vs Fudhi Bajpai And 2 Ors. on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128948221/
1 considered on its own merit.

sentences.text:
3. It is further submitted that on technical grounds the claim petition has been dismissed, especially when the factum regarding the accident was adequately established, hence the findings recorded by the Tribunal on issue nos.1 and 2 is bad in the eyes of law and the claim petition deserves to be allowed.
4.

Shri Rajeev Mishra, learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company has submitted that the Tribunal has appropriately considered the evidence on record and finding various discrepancies in the testimony of the claimant as well as his witnesses, it has dismissed the claim petition especially when the factum of the accident itself was not established by cogent evidence.

The issue of rash and negligent driving would come subsequently but first and foremost it was incumbent upon the claimants to have established that the death of Smt. Siya Dei occurred as a consequence of a motor accident.
When this fact itself was not established the issue as to whether there was any negligence on the part of the driver pales into insignificance.
The appellant has failed to establish the basic facts and the finding recorded by the Tribunal is upon proper appreciation of the evidence, hence the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
5. The Court has considered the rival submissions and before deliberating upon the same the Court finds it necessary to briefly take a glance at the facts.
6. The claimants/appellants had filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Acts before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal which was registered as Claim Petition No.93 of 1999.
It was alleged that Smt. Siya Dei was travelling in a Jeep bearing number U P 35 B/0168 on 28.02.1999.

On account of rash and negligent driving by the driver of the said Jeep, namely, Shiv Kumar Bajpai the accident occurred and Smt. Siya Dei who received injuries and as its consequence she could not survive and passed away.
It was further stated that Smt. Siya Dei was taken to a doctor for treatment but he pronounced her brought dead.
It is in this context that the claim petition claiming as sum of Rs.5,00,000/- as compensation was made.
7. The claim petition came to be contested by the owner and driver of the Jeep and denied all averments.
It was specifically stated that no accident of the vehicle in question i.e. a Jeep bearing number U P 35 B/0168 took place.

It was also alleged that false and fictitious facts have been incorporated only to recover the amount as the vehicle was insured and in absence of any proper evidence the claim itself was not maintainable and was liable to be dismissed.
8. A separate written statement was filed by the Insurance Company contesting the aforesaid plea made in the claim petition.
9. Upon the exchange of pleadings, the Tribunal framed six issues.
However, the relevant issues were issue nos.1, 2 and 4.
In support of the claim, the claimants examined Santosh Kumar as P.W.1 and Kali Shanker as P.W.2.
On behalf of the vehicle owner he examined himself as D.W.1 and the driver was examined as D.W.2.
No evidence either oral or documentary was filed on behalf of the Insurance Company.

sentences.text: The Tribunal while dealing with the issue no.1 considered the testimony of the witnesses and found that there were glaring discrepancies in the statement of the claimants and alleged eye witness who was examined as P.W.2 and since the accident itself was not established the evidence on issue no.1 were returned against the claimant.
However, while dealing with the issue no.2, the Tribunal concluded that the driver of the vehicle bearing number U P 35 B/0168 had a valid driving licence and so also the insurance policy was valid.

The Tribunal also noticed while dealing with the issue no.4 found that the vehicle was being driven by one Nankau who did not have a valid licence and allegedly the defendant no.1 who is alleged to have been driving was incorrect.
With the aforesaid, the claim petition was dismissed.

11. Having taken a glance at the facts and material on record, this Court, at the outset, notices that as per the evidence led by the claimants, it was stated that their mother Smt. Siya Dei was travelling in Jeep No. U P 35 B/0168 from Unnao to Achalganj.

It was also stated that on account of rash and negligent driving of the Jeep driver who dashed against a stationary truck, as a consequence, Smt.
Siya Dei fell from the vehicle and sustained grievous injuries which led to her death.

12. The Tribunal noticed that this statement could not be verified as in the cross examination the claimants witness no.1 clearly stated that they had taken Smt. Siya Dei to the doctor where she was declared as brought dead.
It was stated by the claimants that they had informed the police on the very same day.
However, the record indicated that the FIR was lodged after one month and two days.

The Tribunal also noticed that it could not be ascertained by the claimants regarding the Jeep being present at the accidental site as well as the alleged stationary truck thus the basic fact of the accident between the Jeep and the stationary truck could not be established.

13. The Tribunal also noticed the evidence of the P.W.2 who is alleged to be an eye witness who stated that he knew the deceased since last 25 to 30 years and she was related to him as distant 'Aaji'
(grand mother).
As per his statement, he is said to have witnessed the accident where Smt. Siya Dei had sustained injuries after falling from the Jeep which dashed in a stationary truck.

In his cross-examination he stated that he had first informed the doctor and that he was present at the site with the doctor then he stated that he did not give any information to the police or to the family members of the deceased despite the police station was barely one and half kilometers from the alleged accidental site rather it is the case of the said eye witness that though he had witnessed the accident he went on for his own work without informing the police or family members of the deceased and did not even bother to take her to a doctor/hospital for treatment.

This was found unnatural and unbelievable by the Tribunal as it was not natural for a person to have witnessed an accident where the injured was known and distantly relating and instead of helping or calling for help simply walked away.
14.

This conduct of the said witness coupled with the discrepancies in his statement that he had gone to the doctor, not informing the police and giving another statement that the police had also come to the doctors clinic where Smt. Siya Dei was declared brought dead was not reliable.

15. Another discrepancy noticed was that if the post mortem was done then under what circumstances the FIR came to be lodged after one month and two days could not be explained even Santosh Kumar And 3 Ors. vs Fudhi Bajpai And 2 Ors. on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128948221/
3 in the FIR while the statement were recorded including that of witness while filing the chargesheet the name of P.W.2 Kali Shanker was not included also created a doubt over the statement of the claimant as well as the witnesses.

entities.text: Santosh Kumar And 3 Ors. vs Fudhi Bajpai And 2 Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is in the aforesaid backdrop, the Tribunal recorded a finding that the statement of the alleged eye witness Kali Shanker was not credible and the statement of the claimant apparently who was formal witness as he had not seen the accident nor he could indicate as to how the deceased expired.
16.

In light of the material available on record including the testimony of the claimant witness and in light of the discussions made above, this Court does not find that the findings returned by the Tribunal can be termed as erroneous.

The findings of the Tribunal are based on proper appreciation of the evidence and being a pure finding of fact which could not be pointed out to be perverse, this Court does not find any merit in the appeal which is accordingly dismissed.
Award dated 31.03.2003 passed in Claim Petition No.930 of 1999 is affirmed.
Costs are made easy.
The record of the Tribunal shall be returned forthwith.
